summary.headline: Vishnu Chemicals Q2 FY27 consolidated revenue rose 7.1% YoY to INR429.5 crore, EBITDA up 10% to INR64 crore; management targets 18-19% FY28 EBITDA margin.
summary.overview: Q2 FY27 revenue grew 7.1% YoY to INR429.53 crore and PAT rose 8.2% to INR35.57 crore, with EBITDA margin up to 14.9% from 14.5%. H1 FY27 revenue grew 15.4% and PAT 15.5%, but Q2 growth moderated as West-bound export volumes (mainly leather-linked base chrome cargo) fell on freight disruption linked to West Asia. Shipping and forwarding costs rose to 8.8% of revenue from 5.9% in Q1. Management expects logistics to normalise by Q4 and guided to 17-18% EBITDA margin in FY28 (up to ~20% if chrome ore backward integration and new products deliver), alongside a chrome metal JV and a large capex programme.

segments.name: Chromium chemicals
segments.commentary: Management is shifting mix toward specialty derivatives (chrome oxide green, chromic acid); domestic chromic acid market share cited at 60-70%. Sodium dichromate capacity expansion completed, taking total to 90,000 tons; utilisation over 75%. Chrome oxide green adds ~20,000 tons and chromic acid ~5,000-6,000 tons of incremental capacity.

segments.name: Barium chemicals
segments.commentary: Described as stable cash generator on gross block of ~INR375 crore after completed backward and forward integration; utilisation ~70%; no further barium capex planned. Management is exploring MLCC and battery-related value-added products.

segments.name: Strontium carbonate
segments.commentary: Quarterly contribution similar to last quarter (~INR25 crore previously cited, not updated); customer approvals started in India. Capacity ~12,000 tons per annum, targeting 70% utilisation next year; no EBITDA margin guidance given.

segments.name: Chrome metal JV (50:50 with DCX Chrome, France)
segments.commentary: Greenfield 6,000 tons per annum high-purity chrome metal plant in Visakhapatnam; first-phase production targeted for Q4 FY28. Management indicates EBITDA margin upwards of 20%, with shipments already started to DCX's French facility under a purchase order. Not included in the company's INR520 crore capex figure.

segments.name: DMSO (Dimethyl sulfoxide)
segments.commentary: First organic chemistry venture; 10,000 tons per annum plant expected to commence Q1 FY28, targeting 50-60% operating level in year one, with two to three months of stabilisation. Barium plant supplies a key raw material; raw material is 35-40% of sales.

segments.name: South Africa ore mine
segments.commentary: Mining has started with good output; processing plant (beneficiation) in final commissioning. Shipments to India targeted from Q4 FY27 onward, with FY28 expected to see significant contribution.

guidance_outlook: FY28 consolidated EBITDA margin guided at 17-18%, with management saying 20% is achievable if chrome ore backward integration, DMSO and oxide expansion all deliver.
Chrome ore backward integration expected to start contributing from Q4 FY27; company aims to meet 80-90% of its chrome ore requirement from South Africa.
Export volume recovery expected in Q4 FY27 rather than Q3, as customers typically take 5-6 months to re-contract; management described Q3 as trending better than Q2.
Lost export value from logistics disruption estimated at INR20-30 crore per quarter, mainly base leather-related cargo to the Americas and Europe.

Total capex outlay of INR520 crore: INR190 crore spent, about INR330 crore left, mainly DMSO (~INR250 crore) and chrome oxide expansion (~INR220 crore); a further INR300 crore planned over the next 12 months per one answer.
Peak debt estimated at INR800-820 crore including working capital (INR717 crore currently), with the balance funded from internal accruals.
capex_capacity: Total capex outlay ~INR520 crore; ~INR190 crore spent so far; ~INR330 crore remaining, largely funded by debt with balance from internal accruals.
DMSO plant: 10,000 tons per annum, commissioning Q1 FY28, about INR250 crore capex.
Chrome oxide green expansion: ~20,000 tons incremental; chromic acid: ~5,000-6,000 tons incremental; oxide expansion capex ~INR220 crore.
Chrome metal JV in Visakhapatnam: 6,000 tons per annum, first phase targeted Q4 FY28; separate 50:50 company, excluded from the INR520 crore capex.
Strontium carbonate capacity ~12,000 tons per annum; Vizag plant temporarily shut from 20 October 2026 for maintenance and capex tie-ins after two cyclones, restart planned shortly after the call.
Solar capacity to add ~20 MW, taking solar generation to nearly 6x current levels.
demand_pricing: Export base cargo (leather-linked chrome) hit by freight; logistics cost rose sharply, while chrome oxide, chromic acid, dichromate and barium were not impacted.

Chrome metal India demand estimated at ~2,000 tons, with imports of 1,700-1,800 tons growing 12-13% YoY; management targets 60-70% of JV output for export. Global chrome metal index ~$10.1-10.5/kg (~INR1,000/kg).
Europe seen as relatively strong; a purchase order from European partner for chrome oxide. US market expected to improve by Q4 or early next year.
Receivable days rose to 72-73 days at 30 Sep 2026 from 62 days a year earlier; inventory days also up on logistics and geopolitical uncertainty.
Management flagged raw material and energy cost volatility (sulfur, sulfuric acid, power) as a bigger margin driver than end-market demand.

qa_highlights.question: Have export sales been lost due to supply chain disruption, and by how much?
qa_highlights.answer: Management said the impact is on base leather cargo where freight is 20-25% of selling price; value loss estimated at INR20-30 crore per quarter, with recovery expected by Q4 rather than Q3.

qa_highlights.question: What is the status of strontium carbonate profitability and utilisation?
qa_highlights.answer: Contribution was similar to last quarter with no revenue figure disclosed; customer approvals are coming in India. Utilisation expected at 70% next year; no EBITDA margin guidance given.

qa_highlights.question: What is the chrome metal JV's capex, EBITDA margin and TAM?
qa_highlights.answer: Management gave no capex or precise margin; indicated upwards of 20% EBITDA margin, Indian imports of ~2,000 tons demand, and a 60-70% export target.

qa_highlights.question: Why did receivable and inventory days rise?
qa_highlights.answer: Inventory rise attributed to higher logistics costs and geopolitical uncertainty; receivable days rose to 72-73 from 62 a year earlier, expected to normalise as the environment stabilises.

qa_highlights.question: What is the status of the South Africa ore mine?
qa_highlights.answer: Mining has started with good output; beneficiation plant final commissioning; shipments to India to begin Q4 FY27; FY28 to see significant contribution.

qa_highlights.question: What are the FY28 margin targets and peak debt?
qa_highlights.answer: FY28 EBITDA margin guided at 17-18%, with up to 20% possible; peak debt estimated at INR800-820 crore including working capital.

risks_watch: Freight and logistics cost: shipping cost at 8.8% of revenue in Q2 and export logistics at 20.9% of export sales; normalisation by Q4 is assumed but not guaranteed.
Working capital stretch: receivable days up ~10-11 days YoY to 72-73 days and inventory days higher.

Execution risk on new projects: DMSO start in Q1 FY28 with ramp to 50-60% in year one; chrome metal JV first phase Q4 FY28; South Africa beneficiation plant commissioning and shipments from Q4 FY27 have already slipped in timing.
Leverage rising: peak debt INR800-820 crore against current INR717 crore; debt-to-EBITDA 2.8x at 30 Sep 2026.
Unquantified costs: UAE subsidiary wind-up cost described as not significant; Vizag plant shutdown described as having no business loss.
summary.management_tone: Confident on long-term growth and margin recovery, but cautious on near-term timing: management repeatedly declined to give numbers on lost sales, strontium margins, DMSO and JV economics, and said recovery is "more realistic" in Q4 than Q3.
key_quotes: Definitely, I would say Q4 will be more realistic than Q3 because typically customers look at five to six months of a contract.
I think its gross margins as well as EBITDA margins, even at a 60% operating level are looking very promising.
It is very much possible. I mean, again we'd like to be cautiously optimistic, and it could be -- I mean, our target, I think what was on the horizon is 20% on a consolidated basis.
Probably, this time next year I'll be in a better position to give you a visibility on how things are moving, so.
The positive thing is that we have started getting major approvals from customers in India.

rows.label: Guidance upgrade
rows.why: No explicit revenue growth guidance was given and Q2 revenue growth slowed to 7.1% on freight disruption, with management cautious on near-term timing.

rows.label: Guidance downgrade
rows.why: Logistics normalisation by Q4 FY27 is assumed but not guaranteed, South Africa beneficiation and DMSO timelines have already slipped, and receivable days rose to 72-73 from 62 a year earlier.

rows.label: New product launch
rows.why: DMSO 10,000 t plant expected to commence Q1 FY28 at 50-60% operating level in year one; chrome metal JV first phase targeted Q4 FY28 (6,000 t, EBITDA margin upwards of 20%).

rows.label: South Africa ore mine shipments and chrome ore integration
rows.why: Mining has started with good output and shipments to India are targeted from Q4 FY27, aiming to meet 80-90% of chrome ore needs from South Africa; timing has already slipped once.

rows.label: Chrome metal JV export and Europe demand
rows.why: Management targets 60-70% of 6,000 t JV output for export, shipments to DCX France have started under a purchase order, and Europe is seen as relatively strong; India imports of 1,700-1,800 t growing 12-13% YoY.

rows.label: Receivable and inventory days normalisation
rows.why: Receivable days rose to 72-73 from 62 a year earlier and management expects normalisation as the environment stabilises, but peak debt is guided at INR800-820 crore vs INR717 crore now (2.8x debt-to-EBITDA).

tone.note: Management was confident on FY28 margin recovery, DMSO, chrome ore integration and the chrome metal JV, but cautious on near-term timing and declined to quantify lost export sales, strontium margins and JV economics; analysts pressed on those numbers.
